A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same M-Hyper research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated analyses and reordered theorems.

before.justification: v1 reports original M-Hyper link-prediction results, ablations, efficiency measurements, robustness tests, and case analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline, ablation, decoder-controlled, and embedding-size-controlled comparisons.

M1.justification: The proposed FERF, R2MF, biquaternion scoring procedure, and training losses remain unchanged. The new pseudocode and description of the temperature as learnable provide additional documentation; the decoder variants are experimental comparisons.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate link prediction on DB15K, MKG-W, and MKG-Y, retaining modality-missing, modality-noise, and link-sparsity scenarios. Dataset statistics are identical; the new comparisons change model configurations rather than task or data coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds BiQUE to Table 1 and evaluates MyGO+BiQUE and MoMoK+BiQUE in Table 4. The existing 18 baselines remain. Table 4's MyGO+Tucker and MoMoK+Tucker rows correspond to the previously evaluated MyGO and MoMoK.

E3.justification: Appendix D adds comparisons with matched BiQUE decoder dimensions and matched total embedding sizes of 100 and 800. These introduce additional controls within existing benchmarks; the original splits, filtering, metrics, optimizer, batch size, and hyperparameter search ranges remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis of what produces the gains. Table 2 adds reconstruction-loss removal and M-Hyper+DualE ablations, while Appendix D examines decoder choice and model capacity. Existing robustness, hyperparameter, visualization, and relation-level analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added comparisons continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: All retained scores in Tables 1–3 are unchanged, including M-Hyper MRRs of 41.25, 37.02, and 39.46. v2 substantially adds baseline, ablation, decoder-control, and size-control results. For example, Table 6 newly reports DB15K MRRs of 41.21 and 40.23 at embedding sizes 800 and 100; these are additional settings, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the same pairwise-interaction and information-bottleneck theorems and proofs, reversing their order and renumbering equations. The mathematical definitions and substantive arguments remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The first-hypercomplex-MMKGC novelty claim, fused/independent modality collaboration, and performance and robustness claims remain. Efficiency and theoretical support receive less emphasis in the abstract/conclusion, but the efficiency claim and original theoretical arguments remain elsewhere.

C2.justification: A new Limitations section explicitly restricts applicability to static, transductive graphs and discusses adaptation to changing entities, relations, and modalities. Appendix D adds an interpretation attributing gains to the combined architecture beyond decoder choice or parameter count alone.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data repository link, self-distillation pseudocode with noise-mask sampling, and implementation instructions for the BiQUE-based comparators. It also explicitly identifies the relation temperature as learnable. These extend the available documentation without establishing changes to the original implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Xiao et al. (2025), Pang et al. (2024), and Gong et al. (2026) for potential applications. Section 4.4 also directly credits the already-cited BiQUE work for scoring. The existing related-work discussion remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 updates affiliations, numbers sections, reorders theorems, moves the specific-relation discussion to Appendix C, and adds limitations, end matter, and Appendices D–E.

P2.justification: v2 substantially reformats the document and adds Tables 4–6 and Algorithm 1. Figure 4's panels become vertically stacked, Figure 5 changes from two rows to three, and Figure 6 becomes page-wide. Table 3 moves to the appendix, and the dataset table becomes Table 7.

improvement.justification: The added BiQUE, matched-decoder, and matched-size comparisons better address whether v1's gains reflect architecture, decoder choice, or capacity. Pseudocode and explicit static/transductive limitations also improve reproducibility and interpretation. These are useful, targeted gains; the main results and proofs remain unchanged, and the new comparisons still lack uncertainty estimates.
